instructions: Pat the 1.5 lbs of peeled and deveined shrimp dry with paper towels and transfer them into a large bowl.
Grate the garlic and the 2 tsp of ginger into the bowl. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze one half over the shrimp, about 2 tbsp. Cut the other half into wedges.
Add the chili powder, turmeric, pepper, garam masala and salt. Toss until every shrimp is coated, and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high for a minute. Add 2 tbsp of the coconut oil and half of the curry leaves.

Add half of the shrimp in a single layer. Cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is browned, then flip them and cook the other side for 2 minutes. They're done when they're pink and curled into a loose C. Transfer them to a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp of oil and curry leaves, and cook the rest of the shrimp the same way.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with rice and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Yummy Tummy's Prawns Tawa Fry is the by-name version: shrimp coated in turmeric, pepper, chili, garam masala and lemon, then browned in coconut oil with curry leaves for about 2 minutes a side. Kannamma Cooks roasts the shrimp on a griddle with a ground masala and a cooked onion and tomato, and Shanaz Rafiq's Mangalorean version fries a tamarind and dried-chili masala first. This follows the lead for 1.5 lbs, with a milder chili amount and a 10 minute rest in place of 30 minutes to keep it quick. No tawa prawn page from the trusted Indian cooks exists, and Swasthi's Prawns Fry (4.97 from 52) is a different onion-and-cumin stir fry, so it is not used.
